newsitem.title: USA: NYC Schools Chancellor wants bigger budget - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYC Schools Chancellor wants bigger budget - paper.

text.p: New York City's Schools Chancellor, Rudy Crew, was expected to ask that the Board of Education's $7.8 billion budget be increased by $870.6 million, or 11 percent, split between state and city funds, the New York Times said on Wednesday.
During the first two years that New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani was in office, he cut the board's projected spending by $1.2 billion.

For the next school year, the Chancellor wants an extra $388.4 million, but this is just $54 million more than the mayor had proposed. That extra cost includes $30 million to hire aides to monitor lunchrooms and hallways, the cost estimated for putting in effect a provision in the teachers contract that removes them from this role, the paper said.

The New York City Schools Chancellor also will seek almost $400 million more from Albany than Gov. George Pataki proposed in his executive budget to reduce class sizes, prepare students for state standards and maintain schools.
